newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatari stocks inch up on year-end dividends.
newsitem.headline: Qatari stocks inch up on year-end dividends.

text.p: Share prices at Qatar's unofficial stock market inched up in the week to Thursday as companies said they would distribute higher dividends before their annual general meetings, brokers said.
The Commercial Bank of Qatar's (CBQ) 18-share index edged up 0.82 point to 128.65 from 127.83 points the previous week.
"We saw a second active week in the market," said Mazin al-Shakarchi, CBQ's assistant general manager for treasury and investments.
Six shares advanced in the week to Thursday and 11 were unchanged.
Trading in the shares of market leader Qatar National Bank (QNB) was suspended ahead of its AGM on March 24.
Announcements by QNB and CBQ that they would distribute higher dividends helped boost the market, brokers said.
QNB has announced a pay-out of 25 percent of the capital in cash dividend and one bonus share for every four held.
CBQ has recommended 30 percent of the capital in cash payout and a rights issue inviting shareholders to buy one new share for every two held at 250 riyals against the current market price of 348.
The recommendation is awaiting AGM's approval on March 25.
Qatar Electricity and Water Company has also announced plans to pay out six percent of the capital in cash -- the same as in the previous year.
Gainers included Qatar Navigation which rose 30 riyals to 700, Qatar General Insurance and Al Ahli Bank of Qatar which rose five riyals each to 630 and 255 respectively.
Doha Bank Ltd and Qatar Cinema picked up two riyals each to 310 and 195 respectively and Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Company advanced three riyals to 63.
